Only the **bold lines** are walls; the thin grid lines can be crossed.

1. The robot enters \(P2\), heading right, and reaches \(Q2\).
2. The wall between \(Q2\) and \(R2\) forces it to turn right, so it moves down through \(Q1\).
3. At the bottom of \(Q1\), it turns right again, moving left to \(P1\).
4. The left outer wall blocks it at \(P1\), so it turns right and moves upward through \(P2,P3,P4\).
5. At the top of \(P4\), it turns right and travels across row 4 to \(T4\).
6. At the right edge of \(T4\), it turns right and moves down through \(T3,T2,T1\).
7. At the bottom of \(T1\), it turns right and moves west into \(S1\).
8. The bold wall to the left of \(S1\) blocks that direction, but its right turn—north into \(S2\)—is open.
9. It climbs to \(S4\), turns right, and returns to \(T4\), repeating the same cycle forever.

Thus the robot enters a closed loop and never encounters a position where both straight movement and a right turn are blocked.
